children: shares fell 2.01% to $54.36 at 9:45 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 17, as Nvidia's quarterly holdings report showed its most prominent strategic backer cut its position by a quarter. Nvidia sold 53.7 million shares between July and September, leaving it with 161.1 million. The disclosure lands one day after a new securities suit.

The City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System filed a proposed class action in federal court in San Jose against Intel, CEO Lip-Bu Tan and CFO David Zinsner, Reuters reported. It alleges Intel delayed disclosing how weak PC sales and excess inventory would hit revenue, covering buyers from July 23 to October 29. The complaint points to Intel's mid-August sale of $23 billion of stock at $95 a share. The shares fell 28.6% on October 30 after a soft fourth-quarter outlook.

Nvidia's remaining stake was valued at about $19.4 billion at September 30. At $54.36 it is worth roughly $8.8 billion, a 55% markdown in seven weeks. The share price also sits 43% below Intel's August offering price, which sharpens the plaintiffs' case and could make future equity raises costlier. GuruFocus gives Intel a GF Score of 68/100, with solid profitability offset by a middling balance sheet. Its GF Value of $34.14 puts the shares at a 59% premium, which GuruFocus labels significantly overvalued, so the recovery story is already priced generously. The next test is evidence that PC inventory is clearing in the fourth quarter.

title: Intel Stocks Fall 2.01% as Nvidia Cuts Stake 25% and Shareholders Sue
